title: Two-part evidence items at Grade 3
statement: Whether two-part claim-and-evidence items suit grade 3 is unsettled: state tests reportedly start them a grade later, and reviews of work at that grade disagree.
example: A red team found a two-part evidence item in all 48 generated Grade 3 lessons.
detail: The course plans' red-team taxonomy lists two-part evidence items shipped at Grade 3 as a developmentally inappropriate format, on the ground that state test blueprints put two-part evidence around grade 4 and up, and a red team found one in all 48 generated Grade 3 lessons despite the canonical instruction-quality standard. A later look at the Grade 3 checks found such items still being scored although they are banned at that grade. Against that, a Grade 5 course's acceptance framework records that feedback on the Grade 3 course praised its evidence and two-part work. The blueprint claim is secondhand and is not checked here.
against: The sources quoted disagree with one another. A format record on record keeps two-part items out of Grade 3 and notes that a ruling on them is still pending (choose-the-format-the-target-needs).

evidence.quote: | **Developmentally inappropriate formats** | EBSR shipped at G3 (state blueprints put two-part evidence ~G4+) | format census × grade-level state blueprint |

Also found a few checks pointing the wrong way: option counts capped at a max when the standard sets a minimum, passage length pushed toward STAAR test-prep, EBSR scored when it's banned at G3, and most checks report-only so findings never move a score.
